New: a Prod page that shows what happened and how things are doing, every footer chip one click away again, and session rows that show the branch an agent is really working on.

What's new

- Prod page: a click on the Prod chip opens a page instead of one card. "Now" lists the state, active incidents and alerting monitors. "Performance" shows each health number from your config with its current value, a trend line, its range and the change over the period. "Timeline" lists alerts and recoveries, incidents, deploys and Watchdog stories, newest first; a click opens the item in Datadog. A switch sets the period to 1 hour, 24 hours or 7 days. The page refreshes while it is open and makes no calls while it is closed or the screen is locked.
- Worktree branch on the row: when an agent writes or runs commands in a git worktree, the row shows that worktree's branch with a mark and the folder name, and the uncommitted count, unpushed count, CI mark and pull request follow it. Details shows both: "checked out: X · working in: Y". A subagent in its own worktree shows its branch on its card, and the row adds "+N worktrees". Reading a file in another tree does not switch the row. A removed worktree falls back to the checked out branch.
- Footer chips: Prod, VPN, memory, limit, pull requests and terminals are all visible, in a fixed order, and each opens its panel with one click. A chip that needs a look shows its full wording; when the row is tight it drops its extra words before any chip is hidden.

Fixes

- An open Prod or limit chip no longer shows coloured words on a coloured fill.

Limits

- The timeline cannot show anything older than 7 days or from before the app first ran, and Datadog returns at most 100 events per request.
- Worktree tracking covers Claude Code and Codex sessions. Cursor sessions still show the checked out branch.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

After upgrading, open Setup once and click Set Up so the new Claude Code hook event (folder change) is added. If your Datadog sign-in lacks a permission the Prod page needs, the page names it and only that section stays empty.

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later.
